D=/tmp/morph/order-v7; mkdir -p $D; S=$(date +%s)
cp megatron/storage.py $D/0-$S.py 2>/dev/null
cp tests/test_top_order.py $D/1-$S.py 2>/dev/null
(
 set -e
 venv/bin/python -c "import ast,sys; [ast.parse(open(f).read(), f, feature_version=(3,9)) for f in sys.argv[1:]]" megatron/storage.py tests/test_top_order.py
 venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_top_order.py -q --tb=short
 venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_storage.py tests/test_store_examples.py tests/test_store_upsert.py tests/test_storage_existing.py -q --tb=short
 venv/bin/python decks/v6_guard.py megatron/storage.py --quotes 8 --hashes 3 --tests 0 --lines 79-90 --max 60
 venv/bin/python decks/v6_guard.py tests/test_top_order.py --quotes 0 --hashes 0 --tests-min 5
 R=$PWD
 mut() { T=$(mktemp -d); cp -r megatron tests decks $T/
  $R/venv/bin/python decks/v7_mut.py $1 >> $T/megatron/storage.py
  if cmp -s megatron/storage.py $T/megatron/storage.py; then echo "MUTANT NOT APPLIED: $1"; exit 1; fi
  if (cd $T && $R/venv/bin/python -m pytest $2 -q --tb=no -p no:cacheprovider); then echo "MUTANT SURVIVED: $1 -- $3"; exit 1; fi
  echo "mutant killed: $1"; }
 mut M-O1 tests/test_top_order.py "score-only ordering (v6) passes; a test must save tied rows in an order other than the required one (O.1-O.5)"
 mut M-O2 tests/test_top_order.py "dropping the followers key passes; a test must assert ties on score broken by followers DESC (O.2, O.3)"
 mut M-O3 tests/test_top_order.py "dropping the login key passes; a test must assert equal score and followers broken by login ASC with rows saved out of login order (O.3, O.4, O.5)"
 mut M-O4 tests/test_top_order.py "followers ASC passes; a test must assert the higher-followers row first (O.1, O.2, O.3)"
 mut M-O5 tests/test_top_order.py "login DESC passes; a test must assert login ASC (O.3, O.4, O.5)"
 mut M-O6 tests/test_top_order.py "applying LIMIT before the tie-break passes; a test must cut a tie with n (O.4: top, b, a saved, n=2 -> [top, a])"
 mut M-O7 tests/test_top_order.py "case-insensitive login order passes; a test must assert binary order (O.5: [Bob, alice])"
 venv/bin/python -m pytest tests -q --tb=short --ignore-glob='*.v[0-9].py'
) > $D/acc.log 2>&1; rc=$?; cat $D/acc.log; exit $rc

instruction:
Read docs/TASK_MEGATRON_V7.md FIRST (in your context): section 2.1 gives the BASE record and the table of the 14 tied rows, 2.2 the required order, section 3 the examples O.1-O.5 your tests must prove. Python 3.9-compatible syntax, standard library only, no network in tests; never read experts.db. For the EXISTING file megatron/storage.py: return the whole file; preserve all existing docstrings and comments verbatim; outside lines 79-90 every existing line stays byte for byte (line 77 `def top_experts(db_path, n=10):` and line 78 the type comment included). The acceptance counts triple quotes and comment lines, fails if any removed line is outside 79-90, and caps the file at 60 added / 60 removed lines.

Task 1, megatron/storage.py: in top_experts (lines 79-90) change the query's ORDER BY to `expertise_score DESC, followers DESC, login ASC` (default BINARY collation, no COLLATE), keeping LIMIT ? after it so the tie-break applies before the limit. In the docstring (lines 79-82) keep the text and extend it with one sentence naming the tie-break: followers DESC, then login ASC, independent of insertion order. Nothing else in the file changes: save_experts, existing_logins, _SCHEMA, _COLUMNS stay as they are.

Task 2, tests/test_top_order.py (NEW file): unittest; module docstring naming examples O.1-O.5 of docs/TASK_MEGATRON_V7.md; ONE test method per example O.1, O.2, O.3, O.4, O.5 (O.2 checks all three insertion orders inside one method). Build records as dict(BASE, login=..., expertise_score=..., followers=..., total_stars=...) with BASE copied verbatim from section 2.1; copy the 14-row table as a list literal in the test. Each example uses its own fresh db inside tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(); 'saved in order X' = ONE save_experts(db, [records in that order]) call. Compare login lists with assertEqual against the exact expected list from section 3, every assertion with msg=. Do NOT import helpers from other test files. Import: from megatron.storage import save_experts, top_experts (insert the repo root on sys.path as the other tests do: sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), '..'))).

Output exactly ONE fenced python block per file holding the complete file; the block holds only code -- no '---' line, no file path, no prose inside it; no second block for the same file, no prose before or after.
